articles.title: Wu wins first title since Crucible as Chinese snooker hits new high
articles.summary: Wu Yize claims his first ranking title since he became world champion - a result that means China will have the top two players in the rankings for the first time.
body: Wu Yize secured his first ranking title since becoming world champion with a 10-5 win over Yuan Sijun in an all-Chinese final at the Shenzhen Open.
A profitable week for 22-year-old Wu pushes him to a career high of second place in the world rankings, behind Zhao Xintong.

Wu became the second-youngest player to lift snooker's most coveted title at the Crucible when he beat Shaun Murphy in May, and he followed that up with a composed performance to see off surprise finalist Yuan at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.
Having demolished Judd Trump 6-1 in the semi-finals, Wu had early breaks of 117 and 80 to move 3-1 ahead against Yuan.

articles.title: Djokovic rolls back years to beat Zverev in thriller as Sabalenka swept out in China
articles.summary: Serb into China Open semis after 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 win. Sabalenka loses to 34th-ranked Bartunkova. Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.
body: The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite. He got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.

Boos filled the stadium soon afterwards when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play. The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set. He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.
Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world No 1 dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6, 6-3.

articles.title: ‘Insane’: F1 drivers unite over engine regulations after chaotic Bahrain GP
articles.summary: Antonelli and Hamilton led the criticism in Sepang. Race delayed for 53 minutes after software problems. Formula One’s drivers issued a damning condemnation of the sport’s current engine regulations that caused the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to open with farcical scenes of cars stopping on…
body: Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won in Sepang but only after F1 suffered the embarrassment of a host of cars barely able to complete two formation laps in the wet as they were making their way to the grid.
“It was insane,” said the championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes. “At some point we were five-wide in the straight, because we couldn’t understand what was going on.”

Lewis Hamilton was one of the field who ground to a halt. “I had to stop on-track, stop the car, the engine, and restart it. I’ve never done that before,” he said, while Verstappen reiterated his previous criticism of the engine regulations. “What can you say? It’s not what you want for the sport. I hope there is a lesson learned,” he said.

The issue was caused by software designed to control the engine but which had been insufficiently tested in low-grip, wet conditions which led to what the sport’s governing body the FIA called “an unintended loss of power”.

articles.title: Daryz claims rare back-to-back success in the Arc
articles.summary: Daryz repeats last year's success in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, becoming just the ninth horse to win Europe's richest Flat race more than once.
body: Daryz became just the ninth horse to win the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe for a second time, repeating his 2025 success with a late burst to claim victory in the richest Flat race in Europe.
The Francis-Henri Graffard trained four-year-old became the first colt to double up in the Arc at ParisLongchamp since Alleged did it 48 years ago.
Mickael Barzalona, the winning jockey last year, took the ride again and expertly manoeuvred Daryz through the 16-strong field to hit the front in the closing stages.
The 13-8 favourite needed a photo finish last year but this time claimed victory by more than a length from Bay City Roller (28-1), with Aidan O'Brien's 10-1 chance Diamond Necklace finishing third.

articles.title: Drummond wins mixed doubles title on return to curling
articles.summary: Vicky Drummond marks her return to competitive curling in style, partnering Euan Kyle to an emphatic victory at the Scottish Curling Mixed Doubles Championship.
body: The 33-year-old intensive care nurse left the sport shortly after winning gold at the 2022 Olympics.
Drummond (nee Wright) and Kyle, a bronze medallist from this year's World Championship, won every match they played in Aberdeen this week.
Their 100% run culminated with an 8-1 victory over Katie McMillan and Archie Hyslop in the final, which was over after a mere five ends.
The runners-up lost two of their six group matches but edged out the previously unbeaten partnership of Sophie Jackson and Duncan McFadzean in their semi-final.

articles.title: Evans claims dramatic WRC title after Solberg crash
articles.summary: Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashes in the final moments of Rally Italia Sardegna.
body: Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship (WRC) when he crashed with less than 100 metres to go.
"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans, who became the first British world champion in 25 years.
"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver, he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."
The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

articles.title: Will Jadeveon Clowney return from injury for Week 4 as Texans try to save season?
articles.summary: appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Houston Texans take on the Dallas Cowboys at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 4. Edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney is on the injury report and has been listed as questionable.
body: Clowney was a limited participant at practice for most of the week heading into the Cowboys matchup, making many assume he would be ready to get back on the field. The player with 67.5 career sacks then sat out of Friday’s practice. However, that appeared to be just a precautionary move, as Ian Rapoport is now reporting that Clowney is expected to play today.

The Texans came into the season with championship expectations, but they have fallen to 0-3 through three weeks, so they need all of the help they can get. Clowney, while a backup behind the elite pass rushing duo of Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson, is a big part of what is supposed to be arguably the best defensive unit in the NFL.

So far, Houston’s defense has fallen short. It has really been the offense, and even more so, the injury bug, that has held the team back. While Clowney will return to the field, Azeez Al-Shaair and M.J. Stewart are listed as out, and Logan Hall is questionable. Tank Dell is also on the injured reserve, and Jayden Higgins is out for the season.

articles.title: Djokovic creates more history with epic Zverev win at China Open
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday.
body: The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing.
With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open.

Djokovic is a record six-time champion in Beijing and had won all 29 of his previous matches at the tournament before returning this year for the first time since 2015, when he defeated Nadal in the final to claim his sixth title.
"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn't feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.

articles.title: Daryz retains Arc crown with dazzling display
articles.summary: Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp.
body: Not since the Vincent O'Brien-trained Alleged and Lester Piggott in 1977 and 1978 has a colt managed to defend his title, but once Mickael Barzalona pulled the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz out to make his run the result looked inevitable.

The Prix Foy proved the key form guide, as Daryz beat George Scott's Bay City Roller in that trial and those two filled the same positions again in the main event, with Aidan O'Brien's Diamond Necklace running a fine race in third from stall 16.
Barzalona said: "To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse.
"It was a really tough race, it didn't go as we expected but he showed his talent and that made the difference in the end.

articles.title: Russell 'beyond disappointment' as Wolff 'massively annoyed' by engine failure
articles.summary: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said he was "massively annoyed" after the late unreliability that delivered a potentially knock-out blow to George Russell's title hopes in the Bahrain Grand Prix.
body: Mercedes had already been experiencing an unexpectedly difficult weekend on F1's return to Sepang with the team outqualified by both Red Bull and Ferrari despite bringing a long-awaited car upgrade.

Although Red Bull's Max Verstappen proved too fast in Sunday's chaotic, twice-delayed race, Mercedes were still on course for second with Kimi Antonelli and third with George Russell when, with five laps to go during the second Safety Car phase, the latter's car was stopped by a suspected power unit failure.
The retirement cost Russell 15 points and saw the British driver slip 84 points behind team-mate Antonelli in the title race with seven rounds left.
"I'm so massively annoyed, and not in a happy place," a frustrated Wolff told Sky Sports F1.
